kjv: The great [God] that formed all [things] both rewardeth the fool
mine: Like an archer who wounds everyone is one who hires a passing fool
note: The verse is among the most obscure in Proverbs; rab can be "archer" (Jer 50:29) and mecholel "wounding"; the KJV supplies "God" and reads a theological statement into it. Context: an archer wounding everyone is like one hiring a fool (low confidence). 26:1-12 is a string of fool proverbs; the line is so obscure that no reading is secure.

kjv: a potsherd covered with silver dross
mine: a glaze covering an earthen vessel
note: Hebrew kesef sigim is now usually redivided kesapsagim "like glaze" (Ugaritic spsg), a shiny coat over cheap pottery; the KJV's sense is similar but less precise.
